subject: Urgent: Nexa API p99 spike & end-user errors
messages:
From: Evan Blake <evan@nexaretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nexa Platform Ops <ops@nexaretail.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:14:00Z
Subject: Urgent: Nexa API p99 spike & end-user errors

Vanessa —

We’re seeing a significant p99 latency regression and a sharp increase in 5xx errors across our checkout flows starting ~08:40 UTC this morning. Our telemetry shows:

- p95 latency up from ~320ms to ~2.6s; p99 approaching 6s
- Error rate (5xx) rose from ~0.2% to 3.7%
- Throughput steady, but client-side observed timeouts and repeated retries from our service mesh

This coincides with a rollout of Nexa’s mobile SDK v3.2.1 last night — we’re still investigating whether server or client is the root cause, but the customer-facing impact is material (abandoned checkouts). Attaching a screenshot of our monitoring and a short log extract.

Can Redwood triage immediately? We need an explanation for the regression and a mitigation plan (short-term fallback + longer-term fix). Please advise on next steps and availability for an incident call.

Thanks,
Evan Blake
Head of Platform, NexaRetail

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-12T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: Nexa API p99 spike & end-user errors — initial findings

Vanessa/Team —

I took an initial look at request traces and edge logs. Early findings that narrow the scope:

- Server-side: no recent deploys to the inference fleet between 07:30–09:30 UTC; kernels and quantization profiles unchanged. No memory thrashing on the nodes we own.
- Ingress: short-lived TLS renegotiation errors around 08:38 UTC from a set of client IPs, but not enough to explain the error rate by itself.
- Client amplification: we’re seeing a pattern where many requests with the same correlation id are arriving in bursts — the X-Client-Request header shows ~10× repeated attempts within a short window for a subset of clients.

Attached is a sanitized log snippet that shows repeated inbound requests with identical payloads and rapidly incrementing retry counts. My suspicion: an aggressive local SDK retry/backoff regression (no jitter + immediate retry on timeouts) triggered a retry storm that amplified transient backend latency into sustained p99 spikes.

Suggested immediate mitigations (can be executed in parallel):
- Ask Nexa to temporarily disable the aggressive retry behavior or flip to exponential backoff with jitter (we can provide a 1-line config change).
- On our side, add a per-IP rate limit and abort duplicate requests with identical client request ids for 30s (short mitigation until the SDK patch).
- Instrument and surface a retry metric in the Console for Nexa so they can see amplification in real time.

I can push a short-term ingress filter rule in ~90m and provide a sample SDK patch + config for their engineers. See snippet in attachment for the log lines.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From a business side: this impacted two large accounts and will likely trigger an incident review. Please keep me and my ops team updated on mitigation status and any recommended credits/compensation.

Evan
